PSI UPSILON'S LITERARY ROOTS RUN DEEP
In the early 1800s, literary societies played an important role in the life of college students.
Our Founders, having secured membership in these societies at Union College, valued
opportunities for social interaction which could not be found in the classroom . These
opportunities included reading and writing poetry, discussing literature, and presenting
debates and orations.
Today, with more than 24,000 living alumni, our members have been enriched by the
education and fraternity experience received while attending the leading universities and
colleges in the United States and Canada. So, it should be no surprise that Psi Upsilon has
maintained its literary tradition.
- -
Many of our brothers write and publish literary works on a wide range of subjects.

during the past 12 months. Books published about Psi Us in the past several years are also
featured. The DIAMOND welcomes news of any other new or recent alumni books for
